one_liner: Firedancer's 8- and 16-lane multi-buffer SHA-256 kernels in C; about 2x the Rust sha2 crate on AVX-512 x86.
what_it_does: src/ballet/sha256 in Jump Crypto's Solana validator provides an incremental SHA-256 (fd_sha256_init/append/fini, SHA-NI, Arm SHA2 or RISC-V scalar crypto core), a one-shot fd_sha256_hash, and a batch API: fd_sha256_batch_init, then fd_sha256_batch_add(batch, data, sz, hash) per message, then fd_sha256_batch_fini, after which every 32-byte output is filled. It also offers fd_sha256_hash_32_repeated_batch for advancing many independent hash chains (Proof of History style). The batch API is not a drop-in for a one-call SHA256(): callers must queue independent messages and must not read outputs or change inputs until fini.
how_it_is_fast: Multi-buffer (lane-per-message) SHA-256: up to 8 messages run in the AVX2 lanes (fd_sha256_batch_avx.c) or 16 in the AVX-512 lanes (fd_sha256_batch_avx512.c), so one SIMD instruction advances the compression function of every message at once. Message blocks are loaded in place and transposed (transpose_16x16 / 2x8x8), the padded tail blocks are prepared in a scratch area up front, and the AVX-512 kernel uses vprold rotates and, since PR #11442 (merged 2026-09-13), vpternlogd to fold each round's boolean functions into 4 instead of 12 logic ops. Batches below 5 (AVX-512) or 6 (AVX2) messages fall back to narrower kernels or per-message SHA-NI.
when_to_use: Hashing many independent, similar-sized messages per call on an AVX-512 x86 server, such as Merkle-tree leaves (Solana's 64-shred erasure sets of about 1 KiB each), where it measured about 1.9-2.25x the serial Rust sha2 crate on Zen 4, Zen 5, Emerald Rapids and Granite Rapids.

Advancing 16 or more independent SHA-256 chains (Proof of History style) with fd_sha256_hash_32_repeated_batch, which the header says has higher throughput than the scalar path at fd_sha256_simd_lane_min lanes and above.
C or C++ codebases on Linux x86-64 that can vendor Apache-2.0 code and want a batch hasher without pulling in isa-l_crypto's job-manager API.
Throughput-bound pipelines where per-message latency does not matter (the header warns individual latency can be about 8x worse in the SIMD repeated-hash path).
when_not_to_use: Single messages or small batches: batches under 5-6 messages fall back to SHA-NI or scalar code, so there is no gain over OpenSSL or any SHA-NI hasher.
Zen 1-3 (AVX2 only): the 8-lane AVX path measured 0.93x the serial sha2 crate on an EPYC 7B13, and Firedancer's own header disables the AVX batch implementation when built with -mtune=znver1/2/3.
Non-x86 targets: there is no AArch64 or RISC-V batch kernel; those builds use the per-message reference batch path.
Messages split across buffers (prefix plus payload): each message must be one contiguous (pointer, size) region, so a domain-separation prefix forces a copy that tape-sha256's prefixed API avoids.
Projects that cannot take on Firedancer's build: the code depends on fd_util and the util/simd headers and is selected by Firedancer machine profiles, not a standalone package.

integration.dependencies: Firedancer's fd_util (logging, bit helpers) and util/simd/fd_avx.h and fd_avx512.h headers; built with Firedancer's GNU make machine profiles (config/machine/*.mk)
integration.min_toolchain: GCC 8 is Firedancer's stated minimum (config/machine/linux_gcc_zen2.mk); clang profiles also exist; Linux only, kernel 4.18 or newer to build the project
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 (8-lane) or AVX-512 (16-lane) for the batch kernels; SHA-NI, Arm SHA2 and RISC-V scalar-crypto cores for single-message hashing; generic C elsewhere
integration.thread_safety: Not documented beyond object ownership; each fd_sha256_t or fd_sha256_batch_t is caller-owned state with no locking, so use one per thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the one-shot fd_sha256_hash and incremental API replace a single-buffer SHA-256 call, but the speedup needs the batch init/add/fini API with many independent messages

gotchas: Harness flaw in the only comparison: tape-sha256's merkle_leaves bench calls the internal kernels fd_sha256_private_batch_avx and fd_sha256_private_batch_avx512 directly, bypassing the header dispatch that disables the AVX batch path under -mtune=znver1/2/3; the Zen 3 0.93x row therefore times a kernel Firedancer itself does not select on that CPU (its real API would hash per message with SHA-NI there).

The same harness gates isa-l_crypto's output against sha2 before timing but never checks the Firedancer kernel's digests, so a mis-wired FFI would go unnoticed; Firedancer's own test_sha256.c (extended in PR #11442) checks the batch path against fd_sha256_hash at every size up to 4096 in every lane.

The measured Firedancer build predates PR #11442 (merged 2026-09-13; the Zen 5 run is dated 2026-08-08): that PR reports Zen 4 leaf hashing of a 64-shred FEC set going from 2.92 to 3.53 GB/s, so current Firedancer is likely faster than the published rows (first-party, cross-run figure).

fd_sha256_batch_add does no input validation; output regions must not overlap each other or any message, inputs must stay valid until fini or abort, and abort leaves the outputs in an unspecified state.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over tape-sha256 on Intel AVX-512 parts, where the rival's own runs show Firedancer 2-12% faster, and over isa-l_crypto sha256_mb when you want a synchronous batch call in plain C rather than a job manager; pick tape-sha256 on Zen 3-5 and Apple silicon, and hashtree when the workload is a fixed-shape 64-byte-pair Merkle tree.
verified_claims_summary: In tape-sha256's merkle_leaves bench (64 messages of about 1.05 KiB, one pinned core, best of 15 rounds of 50 iterations), Firedancer's 16-lane AVX-512 kernel ran 12.55 vs 27.71 us per batch on Zen 5, 22.51 vs 43.71 on EPYC 9B14, 21.82 vs 49.18 on Xeon 8581C and 16.89 vs 36.87 on Xeon 6985P-C against the Rust sha2 0.10.9 crate hashing one message at a time with SHA-NI (about 1.9-2.25x, derived from page data), while the 8-lane AVX2 kernel lost on EPYC 7B13 (45.87 vs 42.66 us). Firedancer was built by the rival crate's author from source with unstated compiler version and flags, and no OpenSSL comparison exists.
status_note: Actively developed (batch kernel and bmtree changes merged in September 2026) and Apache-2.0, but the SHA-256 kernels live inside a large validator tree, so reuse means vendoring src/ballet/sha256 plus parts of src/util.
